run.procedureSummary: 1. Charge: add the cycle's charge row to positions 1-6; levels may stand over working volume. 2. Overflow: go through crucibles 1 to 6 in order. Any melt above working volume moves to the next crucible, which receives it before its own check, so overflow can cascade. Overflow from crucible 6 goes to slag. 3. State check, run on the post-overflow melt: BASE at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. SUPERHEATED at or below its lower mark becomes BASE. Otherwise the state holds. 4. Draw-down: work out all six amounts from the post-overflow melt first. BASE gives floor(melt/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED gives floor(melt/2) to crucible i-1, and crucible 1's half goes to slag. Then all six moves happen at once. 5. Emergency tap: if the line total after draw-down is strictly over 38, each crucible keeps floor(melt/2) and the rest goes to slag.

openPoints.point: Which melt level the draw-down amounts use
openPoints.assumption: The post-overflow levels, using the states set in step 3 of the same cycle

openPoints.point: Rule of at most one state change per crucible per cycle
openPoints.assumption: Each crucible is checked once per cycle, in step 3, so this rule never limits anything
The tap fires only above 38, so a total of exactly 38 does not trigger it

openPoints.point: Return-launder melt that leaves a crucible over working volume
openPoints.assumption: It stays there until the next cycle's overflow step. After cycle 5 it stays over, as the write-up says (crucible 2 ends at 10 against a working volume of 8)
Every quarter and half is rounded down, and the remainder stays in the crucible (or goes to slag for the tap)
